action_summary: Round 10 named its own ceiling: seven hand-typed validators decide how much of an unseen environment can be called known. Everything needed to stop typing them was already in the project -- a refusal NAMES A KIND, and a program's verdict on a file IS a judgement about that kind. A judge is now EARNED: admitted only if it separates a real file (written by the program that defines the kind) from a decoy, repeats the verdict, and leaves the tree unchanged. Measured: 7 of 8 earned, the offered set identical to the hand-typed one with 210 judgements across 30 real files and 0 disagreements, and the one refusal is gzip.open(...,'rb') which is LAZY and accepts a decoy -- cat wearing a library call. The ceiling moves: bz2 and xz go from unreadable () to readable after one earn call each, zero new validator code. While auditing round 10's own output I found a real defect in it: all 13 files it called UNKNOWN were accepted by utf8_text, so UNKNOWN was measuring memory's bookkeeping instead of the file; split into KNOWN/UNDERSTOOD/UNREAD and only UNREAD reaches the learning queue.

agent_orientation.earlier_routes_exhausted_reason: Three routes were rejected. (1) Writing more validators by hand: every new environment brings kinds nobody wrote one for, so the set never converges. (2) Composing a judge by guessing an API from a name: measured, gzip.open(p,'rb') is lazy and accepts everything -- 0/0 -- which is cat, and round 10 had already excluded cat for exactly that reason. (3) Trusting a library's declared existence: a module being importable says nothing about whether its verdict discriminates, so existence was refused as evidence.
agent_orientation.independent_verification_note: Producer-run sandbox only: 9 new tests, 23 across the two affected suites. One receipt: 7 of 8 earned, earned set identical to the typed set, 210 judgements on 30 real files with 0 disagreements, the cat-shaped candidate refused 0/0, and bz2/xz made readable in one step with no new code. Also a defect found and fixed in round 10's own verdict (13 UNKNOWN files were all readable). No independent identity has re-run any of it.

No benchmark task was run; no discharge is claimed.
